title: Watch mode: auto-detect and load new frames
description:
## Summary
Hot-reload new frames when they appear in the source directory.

## User Interface
- `--watch` / `-w` CLI flag to enable watch mode on startup
- 'Watch' checkbox in playback controls (next to Loop)
- Ctrl+W keyboard shortcut to toggle watch mode
- Status indicator when watching/scanning

## Architecture

### Loading Phase State Machine
Idle → InitialDiscovery → InitialLoading → Watching → IncrementalLoad → Watching (repeat)

### New Resources
- WatchConfig: enabled flag, poll interval, directory
- LoadingPhase: state machine for loading lifecycle

### Race Condition Mitigations
1. File stability check: Wait for file size to stabilize or file age > threshold before loading
2. Incremental only: Don't replace sequence, extend it with new frames
3. Frame number ordering: Insert new frames in sorted position by frame number

## Implementation Tasks
1. Add WatchConfig resource and --watch CLI flag
2. Add LoadingPhase state machine resource
3. Implement file stability checking in discovery
4. Add Sequence::merge_frames() for incremental insertion
5. Add SequenceAssets::extend_frames() for growing vectors
6. Add watch mode toggle in playback UI
7. Add Ctrl+W keyboard handler
8. Add periodic re-scan system with timer

title: Single load section with draggable range bar
description:
Add visual load section indicator with drag-to-resize.

## Requirements
- Horizontal bar below timeline showing loaded frame range
- Different color for loaded vs unloaded regions
- Draggable left edge: adjusts section start
- Draggable right edge: adjusts section end
- Dragging triggers load/unload of frames

## Data model
- LoadSection { start: usize, end: usize }
- Initially covers estimated max_frames centered on frame 0
- Stored in per-directory seaview.toml

## UI
- Bar spans full timeline width
- Filled region = loaded frames
- Empty/dimmed region = not loaded
- Drag handles at edges (cursor change on hover)
- Tooltip showing frame range

## Behavior
- Drag right edge right: queue frames for loading
- Drag right edge left: unload frames from end
- Same for left edge
- Respect memory budget (can't expand beyond limit)

title: Memory-aware frame loading with timeline UI
description:
## Summary
Implement memory-aware frame loading with a visual timeline showing loaded ranges. This is critical for handling large sequences that exceed available RAM/VRAM.

## Core Requirements

### 1. Global Config (~/.config/seaview/seaview.toml)
- User-level settings separate from per-directory seaview.toml
- Memory budget configuration (auto-detect or manual)
- Default settings that apply across all projects

### 2. Memory Budget System
- Auto-detect available RAM + GPU VRAM
- Calculate reasonable default memory budget (e.g., 50% of available)
- Estimate frame size from first loaded frame
- Compute max frames that fit in budget: `budget / avg_frame_size`
- Only load frames within budget, unload others

### 3. Timeline UI Overhaul
- Fix: slider should reach 100% (current UI bug)
- Playhead indicator: triangle/chevron pointing down at current position
- Loaded range bar: horizontal bar showing which frames are in memory
- Draggable ends: resize loaded range by dragging left/right edges
- Visual distinction between loaded vs unloaded regions

### 4. Load Section Model (Foundation for Multi-Range)
- Data model supports N load sections (ranges)
- Initial UI only uses first section
- Prepare for future: multiple non-contiguous loaded ranges

## Architecture Notes

### Frame Loading Strategy
- Ring buffer style: load frames around current position
- When playhead moves outside loaded range, shift the window
- Or: user manually positions the load window via timeline drag

### State
- `LoadSection { start: usize, end: usize }`
- `Vec<LoadSection>` in config (initially just one)
- `MemoryBudget { limit_bytes: u64, estimated_frame_size: u64 }`

## Checkpoints
1. Global config file support
2. Memory budget estimation and enforcement  
3. Timeline UI fixes (slider 100%, playhead indicator)
4. Single load section with draggable range
5. [FUTURE] Multiple load sections

title: Toast notifications and status bar
description:
Add a toast/notification system for user feedback with status bar.

## Requirements
- Toast notifications that appear briefly then fade (e.g. 'View saved', 'Watch mode enabled')
- Status bar at bottom showing current state (watching, loading progress, etc.)
- Message history accessible via button

## Implementation ideas

- Status bar in bottom panel showing LoadingPhase state + other indicators
- Modal or dropdown for message history

## Complexity
Medium - need new UI components, state management, and wiring to existing events.

title: Unify playback speed: single source of truth
description: The playback speed slider doesn't stick — dragging it causes the value to snap back to 1.0 on the next frame. Root cause is the fragile two-way sync in playback_controls_system (audit Issue 2). sequence_manager.playback_fps (FPS) and ui_state.playback.speed (multiplier) represent the same concept in different units, and the sync heuristic can't tell which side changed. Fix: make ui_state.playback.speed the single source of truth. Have keyboard +/- in handle_playback_input write directly to ui_state.playback.speed instead of sequence_manager.playback_fps. Remove or derive sequence_manager.playback_fps. See docs/audit-visibility-swap-playback.md §4 Issue 2 and §6 Step 2.

title: Unify frame advancement: fix flickering and stutter
description: playback_controls_system overwrites ui_state.current_frame from sequence_manager every frame (audit Issue 3), which can revert frame advances from playback_update_system causing flicker/stutter. Fix: make sequence_manager.current_frame the single source of truth for frame index. All advancement (keyboard, timer, UI buttons) writes directly to sequence_manager. The UI only reads from it for display. See docs/audit-visibility-swap-playback.md §4 Issue 3 and §6 Step 1.

title: Per-directory settings (seaview.toml)
description: Save and load per-directory settings as seaview.toml in the viewed directory. Initial focus: camera position, source coordinates, playback speed, loop toggle. Settings are loaded on startup and saved via UI controls (e.g. Save Camera button).

title: Define Settings struct with TOML serialization
description:
Create a Settings struct in a new settings module (lib/settings.rs):

- camera_position: [f32; 3] (translation)
- camera_rotation: [f32; 4] (quaternion) or [f32; 3] (euler angles - more human-editable)
- source_coordinates: String (yup/zup/fluidx3d)
- playback_speed: f32
- loop_enabled: bool

Use serde + toml crate for serialization. The struct should have sensible defaults via Default trait. Add toml and serde dependencies to Cargo.toml.

title: Load seaview.toml on startup
description:
When seaview opens a directory or file:

1. Resolve the target directory (parent dir if file, dir itself if directory)
2. Check for seaview.toml in that directory
3. Deserialize into Settings struct
4. Insert as a Bevy Resource
5. Apply settings:
   - Camera: set Transform on camera entity
   - Source coords: override CLI default (CLI flag should still win if explicitly set)
   - Playback: set speed and loop on UiState

Precedence: CLI flags > seaview.toml > built-in defaults

title: Save Camera button in UI
description:
Add a Save Camera (💾) button to the playback controls bar:

1. Read current camera Transform (translation + rotation)
2. Load existing seaview.toml if present (preserve other settings)
3. Update camera fields
4. Write back to seaview.toml in the sequence directory
5. Show brief confirmation in UI (e.g. toast/info message)

The button should sit near the existing center-camera (🎯) button. Needs to know the sequence directory path - get from Args resource or SequenceManager.

title: Save playback settings to seaview.toml
description:
Auto-save or manual-save playback settings (speed, loop) to seaview.toml. Options:

- Option A: Save automatically when changed (may be noisy)
- Option B: Save when Save Camera is pressed (bundle with camera save)
- Option C: Separate 'Save Settings' button

Recommendation: Option B - bundle with camera save. The save button becomes 'Save View' and writes camera + playback state together.

title: Global config: ~/.config/seaview/seaview.toml
description:
Add support for user-level global configuration.

## Requirements
- Config location: ~/.config/seaview/seaview.toml (XDG compliant)
- Fallback: ~/.seaview.toml
- Merging: global config provides defaults, per-directory overrides

## Settings to include
- memory.budget_mb: Manual memory limit (optional)
- memory.auto_detect: bool (default true)
- memory.gpu_fraction: f32 (0.0-1.0, how much VRAM to use)
- memory.ram_fraction: f32 (0.0-1.0, how much RAM to use)
- defaults.watch: bool
- defaults.loop: bool
- defaults.speed: f32

## Implementation
- New GlobalSettings struct
- Load at startup before per-directory settings
- Merge logic: per-directory wins if present

title: Memory budget estimation and frame limit
description:
Implement memory-aware frame loading limits.

## Requirements
- Detect available system RAM (sysinfo crate or /proc/meminfo)
- Detect GPU VRAM if possible (wgpu adapter info)
- Calculate memory budget from fractions in config
- Estimate frame size from first loaded mesh (vertex count * stride + index count * 4)
- Compute max_frames = budget / estimated_frame_size
- Enforce limit in SequenceAssets

## New Resources
- MemoryBudget { limit_bytes: u64, used_bytes: u64, frame_estimate: u64 }

## Integration
- After first frame loads, estimate size and compute max frames
- LoadSection respects this limit
- Unload frames outside the section to stay within budget

title: Environment panel: light intensity and color chooser
Night simulation lighting system
description:
Add a configurable lighting system for simulating night-time viewing conditions with adjustable point lights placed above the scene.

Key features:
- N point lights, adjustable via slider
- Grid-based placement with multiple plane-filling algorithms (selectable via chooser)
- Configurable height above sea level (metres), adjustable via slider
- Configurable light throw angle (downward cone angle)

This is useful for visualising fluid simulations under realistic night-time illumination (e.g. flood lighting, search lights).

title: N point lights with grid placement
description:
Spawn N SpotLight entities in a grid pattern above the scene.

- N adjustable via egui slider (e.g. 1–100)
- Grid layout: distribute lights evenly across the scene bounding box
- Lights should be SpotLights (not PointLights) so we can control the cone angle
- Store as a resource (NightLightingConfig) so it's reactive to slider changes
- Despawn/respawn lights when N changes

title: Plane-filling algorithm chooser for light placement
description:
Implement multiple algorithms for distributing N lights across the scene area, with a dropdown selector in the UI.

Algorithms to consider:
- Uniform grid (rows x cols closest to sqrt(N))
- Hexagonal packing (offset rows for better coverage)
- Poisson disk sampling (random but evenly spaced)
- Single row / single column (for directional setups)

UI: egui ComboBox to select the active algorithm. Lights reposition when algorithm changes.

title: Height above sea level slider
description:
Add an egui slider controlling the Y-position (height) of all night lights.

- Label: 'Height (m)' 
- Range: e.g. 5–500m, logarithmic scale might feel better
- Updates all light Transform.translation.y in real time
- Default to something sensible relative to mesh bounding box (e.g. 2x mesh height)

title: Light throw angle (cone angle) slider
description:
Per-light angle widget for controlling cone/throw angle.

Approach: Bevy built-in gizmos for 3D cone visualisation + egui panel for per-light controls.

Each light gets:
- A 3D cone wireframe gizmo (Gizmos::circle at the base + lines to apex) showing throw coverage
- An egui slider in a lighting panel for its angle (5°–180°)
- Gizmo updates in real time as slider changes

Future: consider transform-gizmo-bevy v0.8.0 (Bevy 0.16 compatible) for drag-to-position lights in the viewport.

No new crate dependencies needed for initial implementation.

title: Desktop integration: .desktop file, MIME types, icon
description:
Create Linux desktop integration for Seaview:

## Tasks
1. Create application icon (SVG and PNG at multiple sizes)
2. Create .desktop file for GNOME/freedesktop
3. Register MIME types for .stl, .gltf, .glb files
4. Create install script to set up desktop integration

## Files to create
- assets/icons/seaview.svg (vector icon)
- assets/icons/seaview-{16,32,48,128,256}.png (raster icons)
- scripts/seaview.desktop (desktop entry)
- scripts/seaview-mimetypes.xml (MIME type definitions)
- scripts/install-desktop.sh (installation script)

## Installation locations
- ~/.local/share/applications/seaview.desktop
- ~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/{size}/apps/seaview.png
- ~/.local/share/mime/packages/seaview-mimetypes.xml

close_reason: Phase 1 complete: LightingSettings, MaterialSettings, EnvironmentSettings bridge structs with From conversions, Settings expanded with cameras HashMap + active_camera + environment, migration logic for old [camera], 26 unit tests all passing

If environment.lighting present, build NightLightingConfig and insert_resource. If environment.materials["fluid"] present, build MaterialConfig and insert_resource.

Full save->quit->relaunch round-trips all values including named cameras. Materials map with unknown keys preserved on merge.

title: Check and fix font size in sidebar
[FUTURE] Multiple load sections for non-contiguous playback
description:
Support multiple non-contiguous load sections.

## Deferred - build on single section first

## Concept
- User can define multiple ranges to keep loaded
- Playback skips unloaded regions or pauses at boundaries
- Useful for comparing specific timesteps without loading everything

- Visual gaps between sections
- Section list/management panel

- Memory budget system
